title: Vayelech: Moses went (Deuteronomy 31:1)
hookLine: at the end, Moses goes out to the people rather than calling them in
tomorrow: Vayelech: strong and of good courage (Deuteronomy 31:7)

cards: You're called into the office. You wait outside a door. You're given a time slot.
When an important person wants to speak with you, you usually go to them; leaders summon. At the very end of his life, Moses leads the whole camp.
He could have every tribe brought before his tent, and nobody would have blamed him for it. The portion opens with him doing the opposite.

teach.b: "And Moses went and spoke these words unto all Israel." In Hebrew, vayelech Moshe: and Moses went.
Readers ask: went where? He wasn't on a journey. The text doesn't say.
So the commentators fill the silence, each a little differently.

teach.h: TRIBE BY TRIBE, TO SAY GOODBYE.
teach.b: Ibn Ezra suggests he went from tribe to tribe through the whole camp, to tell each one in person that he was about to die, and to strengthen them.
Nachmanides pictures him going out to the people the way someone about to leave goes to say goodbye to a friend, as a mark of respect.
Either way, the man who spoke with God doesn't call the people in for one final address. He walks to them.

teach.h: A HUNDRED AND TWENTY, STILL GOING.
teach.b: In the very next verse he tells them why he's saying goodbye: "I am a hundred and twenty years old this day; I can no more go out and come in."
And still, he goes out to them one more time. The portion named for this moment, Vayelech, is short: one chapter, thirty verses. Maybe that fits.
A last visit doesn't need to be long. It needs to happen. A leaving can be done by announcement, by a notice on the wall.
Moses chooses to do it in person, tent by tent.

how: Vayelech is read in the fall, near Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur, and is often paired with Nitzavim; teachers draw from its opening the value of a leader going out to the people.

o: and he blessed: Moses' final gift
and he went: the portion's first words
and he spoke: Moses' farewell address

games.q: inside and he went — tap the pairs.

s: the text says exactly where Moses went
it's silent; the commentators fill it in.
Vayelech is a single chapter of the Torah
Moses summoned the people to his tent for his farewell
the text says he went to them.

games.q: you're Moses, a hundred and twenty, about to die, with the whole camp to address. what does the text say you do?
o: go out to the people yourself.
games.why: and Moses went: the leader of the whole camp walks to the people to say goodbye.

practice: Think of someone you've been waiting to hear from: a friend who's gone quiet, a relative you only see when they visit you, a neighbor you'd talk to if only they knocked.
Picture reversing it, walking to their door or sending the first message, not a summons but a visit, and see their face when it's you who came.

wordCard.voice: Vayelech. And he went. The first word of a short portion, one chapter long.

orig.note: Hebrew: and he went. the first word of Deuteronomy 31 and the name of the portion.

carryVoice: Your line: he went to them. A last visit doesn't need to be long. Five hundred twenty-two days now.
